_comment: Regression targets for the on-device DSP, taken from the Python reference
implementation that was validated against human breath counts.
The rates in 'rate_bpm' are what the reference produced on the same
recording with the same window. They are not ground truth: the counted
truth is in 'counted_bpm' where a human counted, and the reference itself
is only accurate to about +/-4 /min. What this file pins down is that the
C port still agrees with the reference it was derived from, so that a
change to the firmware's signal processing cannot silently drift.
void_collect is the control that matters most: an empty room must never

cases.name: cat at 63 cm, full 180 s
cases.note: Reference run over the whole recording.

cases.name: cat at 63 cm, 60 s, human-counted
cases.note: Counted live at 26, corrected to about 28 by the observer.

cases.name: blind trial 1, undisclosed distance
cases.note: Estimate ran 3.5 /min low against the count.

cases.name: blind trial 2, undisclosed distance
cases.note: Estimate ran 4.4 /min low; the count may include extra breaths.

cases.name: resting adult at 60 cm
cases.note: Human band. Displacement is two orders of magnitude above the cat.

cases.name: cat asleep at 74 cm
cases.note: A deeply asleep cat: 29.7 /min at 14 dB with 100 % window agreement, and the same animal that measured 28-30 /min on the bench weeks earlier. It is here because it was briefly REJECTED: depth was being read from the reference row, which is chosen for phase coherence rather than strength, and landed on a row holding 2.9 um while the row that saw her held 59.7.

cases.name: cat that moved mid-window
cases.note: A human counted 35 breaths in this window but reported the cat was only still for the first 26. The settled portion measures 33.7 /min at 39 um; the last 18 seconds of movement reach 166 um and drag the whole-window estimate to 19.7 /min. Before the motion ceiling this was reported as ok at 67 % stability - a plausible rate, wrong by fourteen.

cases.name: empty room, low-amplitude interference
cases.note: Captured live from a deployed device in an empty room. It reports 57 /min at 100 % stability and 13.4 dB - a higher SNR than a real cat - because stability and SNR are both scale-invariant. Narrowed to the subject's band it fails on SNR as well, and on amplitude: 7.7 um against 45.8 for the weakest real animal. Run at the default 12-66 band this same recording is still reported as breathing, which is why the tuning guide says to narrow the band to the subject.

cases.name: empty room, the control
cases.note: Only 45 s long, so fewer than three stability windows form and no verdict is offered. With three windows forced it scores 33 %, against 80-100 % for a breathing animal.
